title: Sort List
description:
Given the `head` of a singly linked list, return the list after sorting it in **ascending order**.

If the list is empty (`null`), return `null`.

Follow-up: Can you sort the linked list in `O(n log n)` time and `O(1)` auxiliary memory space?
constraints: The number of nodes in the list is in the range [0, 5 * 10^4].
hints: Merge sort is ideal for linked lists because merging two sorted lists takes O(1) extra space by re-linking pointers.
A top-down merge sort splits the list at the midpoint with fast/slow pointers, running in O(n log n) time and O(log n) recursion stack space.
To achieve true O(1) auxiliary space, use bottom-up iterative merge sort: merge adjacent sublists of size 1, then size 2, then size 4, and so on until the block size reaches the list length.
